resources.string: Lets a paired computer control this phone: shows a cursor when your mouse moves onto the phone, taps, drags, scrolls and performs system actions (home, back, recents, volume, media). This service cannot read what is on your screen. Typing from your computer uses the separate, optional \"AirBridge Typing & Clipboard\" service.

Optional. Lets a paired computer type into the text field you are using (and use Enter, Backspace, Tab, arrows, copy, cut, paste and select all), and notices when you copy so the text can go to your computers automatically. To do this it can read the focused text field and the label of a button you tap (such as \"Copy\"), and it types like a keyboard. AirBridge does not store or upload screen content; only your clipboard goes to your own paired devices. Banking and UPI apps may warn about accessibility services that can read the screen: switch this off while paying. Remote control works without it.
Pause remote control while a payment app is open

Banking and payment apps, such as Paytm, PhonePe and Google Pay, refuse to take a payment while any accessibility service is switched on, and remote control is one. With this on, AirBridge switches remote control off when one of those apps is in front and back on when you leave it. It also switches remote control off when none of your computers has been connected for a minute, and back on when one connects.
Lets AirBridge see which app is in front, only to notice a payment app. Without it AirBridge can\'t tell when you open one, and your payment may be blocked.

Android only lets AirBridge switch remote control back on by itself if you give it a special permission, and only a computer can give it. It takes a one-time setup, about 10 minutes. Without it, you turn remote control on again yourself after each payment, and AirBridge can\'t switch it off when no computer is connected.
It was switched off for a payment app. Tap to turn it back on.
It went off when AirBridge was updated. Tap to turn it back on.
